note: Both sets bind the detector, filter, and coronagraph values correctly and both repeat the guide-channel magnification claim verbatim. Set A additionally extracts two correct Table 5.5-4 entries for the UV Science channel (UV bandpass 0.2–0.45 µm science and Visible bandpass 0.45–0.67 µm science) that Set B omits entirely. Since Set B's shown claims are otherwise identical to Set A's, Set A is strictly better, with the same duplicate-claim flaw in both.
remarks: Both sets repeat the guide-channel magnification claim (32 pixels across the telescope aperture) twice. Both also leave out several facts on the page: the IR bandpass row of Table 5.5-4 (1.6–1.8 µm guide, 0.975–1.8 µm science), the Visible Science channel bandpasses (0.3–0.45 and 0.45–1.0 µm), the fixed field stop value of 4" (only the 'slightly larger' relation is captured), and the Saphira/HgCdTe sensor identity and 60K dark-current rationale. The 'Guide filter' entity is somewhat vague — it is the UV bandpass guide-mode filter of the IR Science column.
